sourceReview: Read bundled BSB Psalm 147 in full with each verse's related passages before drafting. References are thematic or literary comparisons, not an invented historical occasion. Scripture is never stored in the notes; it loads from the bundled BSB.

study.title: He heals the brokenhearted
study.intro: Psalm 147 praises God who is both infinitely great and intimately caring. The same LORD who counts and names every star also heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds. He rebuilds Jerusalem and gathers its exiles, sends rain and feeds young ravens, and controls snow, frost and hail with a word. Most wonderfully, He has given His word to His people. The psalm calls Jerusalem to praise Him.
study.context: Psalm 147 likely comes from after the exile, when Jerusalem's walls were rebuilt and scattered Israelites were gathered home (Nehemiah 12:27-43). It falls into three movements, each opening with a call to praise (verses 1, 7, 12). The ancient Greek translation divides it into two psalms. It contrasts God's delight in the humble and those who hope in Him with His lack of interest in military strength.
study.peopleNote: No author is named. Jerusalem's returning exiles, the brokenhearted and the humble are in view. Jacob and Israel name God's people. God is never portrayed as a human figure in planned art.

verses.title: Good to sing praise
verses.heading: How pleasant and lovely to praise Him
verses.meaning: 'Hallelujah! How good it is to sing praises to our God, how pleasant and lovely to praise Him!' Praise is not a duty forced on us; it is good for us and a delight. Singing to God lifts the heart, focuses the mind and puts life in perspective. Like a beautiful view or a good meal, praise is pleasant. God made us to find joy in worshiping Him.
verses.context: Psalm 92:1 says it is good to give thanks to the LORD and sing praises to Your name. Psalm 135:3 says sing praises to His name, for it is lovely. Colossians 3:16 urges singing with gratitude in your hearts to God.
explore: Pleasant
Delightful and agreeable, bringing enjoyment and satisfaction to the heart.
Lovely
Fitting and beautiful, right and good in a way that brings delight.
verses.reflect: When has praising God felt good and lovely to you? What made it so?
verses.alt: Musicians and singers on temple steps at golden morning light.

verses.title: Builder and gatherer
verses.heading: He gathers the exiles of Israel
verses.meaning: 'The LORD builds up Jerusalem; He gathers the exiles of Israel.' God is rebuilding what was destroyed and bringing home those who were scattered. After the exile, Jerusalem's walls lay in ruins and Israel's people were spread across foreign lands. God restored both. He is still the God who rebuilds broken lives and gathers lost people home.
verses.context: Nehemiah 2:17 describes rebuilding Jerusalem's walls. Isaiah 11:12 promises God will assemble the scattered of Judah from the four corners of the earth. John 11:52 says Jesus died to gather the scattered children of God into one.
explore: Builds up
Rebuilds and restores what was broken down, making it strong again.
Exiles
People forced to live away from their homeland, scattered among foreign nations.
verses.reflect: What in your life needs God to rebuild it? What scattered part needs gathering home?
verses.alt: Workers rebuilding a city wall stone by stone at sunrise.

verses.title: Healing broken hearts
verses.heading: He binds up their wounds
verses.meaning: 'He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.' This is one of the most tender verses in Scripture. God does not just repair walls; He repairs hearts. Like a doctor bandaging a wound, He gently cares for those crushed by grief, betrayal or loss. Broken hearts are not too much for Him. He heals them, sometimes slowly, but truly.
verses.context: Isaiah 61:1 says the Messiah is sent to bind up the brokenhearted, which Jesus read in Luke 4:18. Psalm 34:18 says the LORD is near to the brokenhearted. Ezekiel 34:16 says God will bind up the injured.
explore: Brokenhearted
People crushed by grief, loss, betrayal or deep disappointment.
Binds up
Wraps and bandages wounds to protect them and help them heal.
verses.reflect: Where is your heart broken? Invite God to bind up that wound.
verses.alt: Hands gently wrapping a bandage around another person's arm in lamplight.

verses.title: Naming the stars
verses.heading: He calls them each by name
verses.meaning: 'He determines the number of the stars; He calls them each by name.' Right after healing hearts, the psalm looks up at the stars. God knows how many there are, billions upon billions, and has a name for each one. The God who handles the universe in such detail also cares about the details of your broken heart. Greatness and tenderness belong together in Him.
verses.context: Isaiah 40:26 says God brings out the starry host one by one and calls them each by name. Genesis 15:5 has God telling Abraham to count the stars. Luke 12:7 says even the hairs of your head are numbered.
explore: Determines the number
Counts and sets the exact number, knowing every one completely.
Calls by name
Knows individually and personally, as a shepherd knows each sheep.
verses.reflect: How does knowing God names every star help you trust His care for you?
verses.alt: A dense field of stars over a dark desert horizon.

verses.title: Unlimited understanding
verses.heading: His understanding has no limit
verses.meaning: 'Great is our Lord, and mighty in power; His understanding has no limit.' God is great in size, strong in power and endless in wisdom. There is nothing He does not understand, including you and your situation. When you cannot make sense of life, you can rest in knowing that God's understanding has no ceiling.
verses.context: Isaiah 40:28 says His understanding is beyond measure. Romans 11:33 praises the depth of God's wisdom and knowledge. Job 37:5 says God does great things beyond our understanding.
explore: Mighty in power
Having great strength and ability, able to do anything He wills.
No limit
Without end or boundary; infinite and beyond all measurement.
verses.reflect: What situation do you need to trust to God's unlimited understanding?
verses.alt: A vast canyon stretching into the distance under clear sky.

verses.title: Lifting the humble
verses.heading: The LORD sustains the humble
verses.meaning: 'The LORD sustains the humble, but casts the wicked to the ground.' God lifts up those who are lowly and humble, and He brings down the proud and wicked. His kingdom turns the world's values upside down. The humble are not losers; they are the ones God holds up. Pride may look strong for a while, but it ends in a fall.
verses.context: Luke 1:52 says He has brought down rulers and lifted up the humble. James 4:10 says humble yourselves before the Lord and He will lift you up. Proverbs 16:18 says pride goes before destruction.
explore: Sustains
Holds up, supports and keeps someone going when they are weak.
Humble
Lowly in heart, aware of one's need of God and not proud.
verses.reflect: Where do you need God to lift you up as you humble yourself before Him?
verses.alt: A shepherd helping a weary traveler up onto a rocky path.

verses.title: Thanks with the harp
verses.heading: Make music on the harp to our God
verses.meaning: 'Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving; make music on the harp to our God,' The second movement begins with another call to praise. This time it is thanksgiving with music. Thanks is the right response to all God has done. Instruments and voices together express what words alone cannot. Gratitude set to music fills both heart and room.
verses.context: Psalm 33:2 says praise the LORD with the harp. Psalm 95:2 says come before Him with thanksgiving and songs. Ephesians 5:19-20 urges singing and making music to the Lord, always giving thanks.
explore: Thanksgiving
Expressing gratitude to God for His gifts and acts.
Harp
A stringed instrument plucked by hand, used in Israel's worship.
verses.reflect: What could you thank God for in a song or hymn today, even a simple one?
verses.alt: A young woman playing a lyre in a courtyard at evening.

verses.title: Clouds, rain and grass
verses.heading: Who makes grass to grow on the hills
verses.meaning: 'who covers the sky with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass to grow on the hills.' God runs the water cycle. He gathers clouds, sends rain and makes grass grow even on rocky hillsides. Weather is not random. Every rainfall is His gift to the land, and every green hill shows His care.
verses.context: Job 38:25-27 describes God sending rain on uninhabited land to make grass sprout. Acts 14:17 says God gives rain from heaven and fruitful seasons. Psalm 104:13-14 says He waters the mountains and makes grass grow for cattle.
explore: Prepares rain
Gets rain ready and sends it, as God plans the weather for the land.
Hills
Rocky high ground in Israel where grass is hard to grow without rain.
verses.reflect: Next time it rains, how might you see it as a gift from God?
verses.alt: Rain clouds over green hills with sheep grazing below.

verses.title: Feeding young ravens
verses.heading: For the young ravens when they call
verses.meaning: 'He provides food for the animals, and for the young ravens when they call.' Ravens were unclean birds in Israel, not valued by people. Yet God hears their young calling for food and feeds them. If God cares for ravens, how much more does He care for you? Jesus made exactly this point to His anxious disciples.
verses.context: Jesus said in Luke 12:24, 'Consider the ravens: they do not sow or reap... yet God feeds them. How much more valuable are you!' Job 38:41 asks who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God.
explore: Ravens
Large black birds considered unclean in Israel, yet fed by God.
Provides
Supplies what is needed, giving food, shelter and daily care.
verses.reflect: What worry could you release, knowing God feeds even young ravens?
verses.alt: Young ravens in a nest with open beaks on a rocky ledge.

verses.title: Not impressed by strength
verses.heading: He does not delight in the strength of the horse
verses.meaning: 'He does not delight in the strength of the horse; He takes no pleasure in the legs of a man.' Horses were the strongest military power of the day, and a fast runner was a prized warrior. But God is not impressed by human strength or athletic ability. The things the world admires most are not what delight Him most.
verses.context: Psalm 33:16-17 says a horse is a false hope for victory. 1 Samuel 16:7 says the LORD looks at the heart, not appearance. Isaiah 31:1 warns against those who rely on horses instead of the Holy One of Israel.
explore: Strength of the horse
The power of war horses and chariots, the military might of ancient armies.
Legs of a man
The speed and power of a trained warrior or a fast runner.
verses.reflect: What strength or ability do you rely on that God may not value as much as you think?
verses.alt: A war horse standing alone in an empty field at dusk.

verses.title: What pleases God
verses.heading: Who hope in His loving devotion
verses.meaning: 'The LORD is pleased with those who fear Him, who hope in His loving devotion.' Here is what delights God: not strength but reverence and hope. He takes pleasure in people who honor Him and who trust His steadfast love. Anyone can do this, regardless of their physical abilities. God's pleasure rests on a heart that looks to Him.
verses.context: Psalm 33:18 says the eye of the LORD is on those who fear Him, who hope in His loving devotion. Hebrews 11:6 says without faith it is impossible to please God. Micah 6:8 says God requires us to walk humbly with Him.
explore: Pleased
Delighted, finding joy and satisfaction in someone.
Fear Him
Revere God with awe, honoring and trusting Him above all.
verses.reflect: How does knowing God is pleased by your hope in Him change how you see yourself?
verses.alt: A woman sitting peacefully at a window looking out at the dawn.

verses.title: Praise, O Zion
verses.heading: Exalt the LORD, O Jerusalem
verses.meaning: 'Exalt the LORD, O Jerusalem; praise your God, O Zion!' The third movement begins with a call to the city itself. Jerusalem, rebuilt and repopulated, should lift up the LORD. Every restoration is a reason to praise. God's people today are also called to exalt Him for every way He has rebuilt and restored them.
verses.context: Psalm 48:1 says great is the LORD and greatly to be praised in the city of our God. Isaiah 52:9 says break forth into joy, ruins of Jerusalem. Hebrews 12:22 speaks of the heavenly Jerusalem.
explore: Zion
The hill of Jerusalem where the temple stood, standing for God's people.
Exalt
To lift high in honor and praise, giving someone the highest place.
verses.reflect: What restoration in your life or community calls for praise to God?
verses.alt: A crowd gathered in Jerusalem's streets with arms raised in celebration.

verses.title: Strong gates, blessed children
verses.heading: He strengthens the bars of your gates
verses.meaning: 'For He strengthens the bars of your gates and blesses the children within you.' God secures the city and blesses its families. Gate bars kept enemies out, and children inside could grow up in safety. Security and family blessing come from God. When we pray for our homes and communities, we can ask Him for both protection and blessing.
verses.context: Nehemiah 3:3 describes setting the doors, bolts and bars of Jerusalem's gates. Psalm 127:1 says unless the LORD protects the city, the watchmen stand guard in vain. Psalm 128:3 pictures children around the table.
explore: Bars
Heavy wooden or metal beams that lock a gate shut against attack.
Within you
Inside the city walls, among its people and families.
verses.reflect: How can you pray for God's protection and blessing over your home?
verses.alt: A heavy wooden gate barred shut with children playing safely inside.

verses.title: Peace and finest wheat
verses.heading: He fills you with the finest wheat
verses.meaning: 'He makes peace at your borders; He fills you with the finest wheat.' God gives peace from enemies and food in abundance. The 'finest wheat' is literally 'the fat of the wheat,' the very best. When God provides, He does not give leftovers. Peace and plenty are signs of His care for His people, gifts to receive with gratitude rather than take for granted.
verses.context: Psalm 81:16 says God would feed Israel with the finest wheat. Isaiah 60:18 promises no violence within your borders. Philippians 4:7 speaks of the peace of God guarding hearts.
explore: Borders
The boundaries of a land, where enemies might attack.
Finest wheat
The best quality grain, a picture of rich abundance.
verses.reflect: Where do you need God's peace at your 'borders' today?
verses.alt: Golden wheat fields waving in the breeze near a peaceful town.

verses.title: His word runs swiftly
verses.heading: His command to the earth
verses.meaning: 'He sends forth His command to the earth; His word runs swiftly.' God's word is like a messenger running at full speed. When He speaks, creation obeys immediately. Nothing slows His word down. The same word that commands the weather also speaks to us in Scripture. It is alive, active and powerful, and it still accomplishes what He sends it to do.
verses.context: Isaiah 55:11 says God's word will not return empty. Hebrews 4:12 says the word of God is living and active. Genesis 1:3 shows creation responding instantly: 'Let there be light,' and there was light.
explore: Command
An order given with authority, expecting to be obeyed.
Runs swiftly
Moves quickly, like a messenger racing to deliver news.
verses.reflect: How might God's word be running swiftly to you today through Scripture?
verses.alt: A messenger running along a road across open hills.

verses.title: Snow like wool
verses.heading: He spreads the snow like wool
verses.meaning: 'He spreads the snow like wool; He scatters the frost like ashes;' The psalm paints winter beautifully. Snow covers the land like soft white wool. Frost scatters like fine gray ashes. Even cold seasons are God's handiwork. Winter is not a sign of God's absence but of His creativity and control, and it prepares the ground for spring.
verses.context: Snow occasionally falls in Jerusalem's hills. Job 37:6 says God tells the snow, 'Fall on the earth.' Isaiah 1:18 says though your sins are like scarlet, they will be white as snow.
explore: Wool
Soft white sheep's fleece, a picture of fresh snow's softness.
Frost
Thin ice crystals that form on surfaces in cold weather.
verses.reflect: What 'winter' season might God be working in, even if it feels cold?
verses.alt: Fresh snow covering a hillside village like a soft blanket.

verses.title: Hail and icy blast
verses.heading: Who can withstand His icy blast?
verses.meaning: 'He casts forth His hail like pebbles. Who can withstand His icy blast?' God throws hail like handfuls of pebbles. The cold He sends is fierce, and no one can stand against it. This reminds us of God's power over nature. We cannot control the weather, but He can. That is both humbling and comforting.
verses.context: Exodus 9:23-26 describes the plague of hail on Egypt. Joshua 10:11 tells of hailstones falling on Israel's enemies. Job 38:22-23 speaks of the storehouses of hail reserved for times of trouble.
explore: Hail
Balls of ice falling from storm clouds, sometimes large and destructive.
Withstand
To stand firm against something without being overcome.
verses.reflect: How does God's power over nature help you trust Him with things you can't control?
verses.alt: Hailstones bouncing on a stone courtyard under dark clouds.

verses.title: The thaw
verses.heading: He sends forth His word and melts them
verses.meaning: 'He sends forth His word and melts them; He unleashes His winds, and the waters flow.' With another word, God brings the thaw. Ice melts, warm winds blow and streams run again. Every winter ends at His command. This is a picture of hope: frozen situations can thaw when God speaks. What seems stuck can begin to flow.
verses.context: Song of Solomon 2:11-12 says the winter is past, the rains are over, flowers appear on the earth. Isaiah 43:19 says God makes rivers in the desert. Lamentations 3:22-23 speaks of new mercies.
explore: Melts
Turns ice and snow into flowing water through warmth.
Unleashes
Releases with force, letting something powerful go free.
verses.reflect: What frozen situation in your life do you need God to thaw?
verses.alt: Melting snow running into a stream as green grass appears.

verses.title: His word to Jacob
verses.heading: He declares His word to Jacob
verses.meaning: 'He declares His word to Jacob, His statutes and judgments to Israel.' Here is the greatest gift. The God who commands weather has also spoken personally to His people. He gave Israel His word, laws and guidance. Creation hears God's command; His people hear His covenant word. To have God's word is a privilege.
verses.context: Deuteronomy 4:8 asks what nation has such righteous laws as this. Romans 3:2 says the Jews were entrusted with the oracles of God. Psalm 119:105 says Your word is a lamp to my feet.
explore: Statutes
Fixed rules and decrees given by God for His people's life.
Judgments
God's rulings and just decisions that guide right living.
verses.reflect: How can you treasure God's word as a gift this week?
verses.alt: An open scroll resting on a table near a lamp.

verses.title: A unique privilege
verses.heading: He has done this for no other nation
verses.meaning: 'He has done this for no other nation; they do not know His judgments. Hallelujah!' Israel received something unique: God's revealed word. Other nations had no such gift at that time. This privilege calls for praise, not pride. In time, God would send His word to all nations through the gospel, so every people could know Him.
verses.context: Deuteronomy 4:7-8 marvels at Israel's privilege. Acts 14:16 says in past generations God let nations go their own way. Matthew 28:19 sends the gospel to all nations.
explore: Privilege
A special honor or advantage given to some and not others.
Judgments
God's laws and rulings showing how to live rightly.
verses.reflect: How can you share the gift of God's word with someone who doesn't know it?
verses.alt: Pilgrims carrying scrolls along roads leading out toward distant lands.
